text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Listed fertiliser maker Azomures dismissed 200 staff due to declining sales.
- Oversupply in the real estate sector depressed prices by up to eight percent, the Romanian association of real estate agents said.
- The National Bank's hard currency reserve stands at more than $1.5 billion.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- U.S. helicopter maker Bell Helicopters is expected to buy a majority stake in local plane maker IAR on Wednesday.
- Foreign investors look at Romanian ball bearing makers, according to capital market sources quoted by the newspaper.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The government is expected to discuss on Sunday draft amendments to the foreign investment law to include provisions on portfolio investment. The tax on capital gains is expected to be four percent.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Prices for accommodation and meals in Black Sea resorts have been on the rise and many Romanians will have to go on their holidays offseason.
ADEVARUL
- An international consumer goods fair opens in Bucharest on Thursday. More than 650 companies from 28 countries are expected to attend.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Four of the six miners injured in this week's explosion at the Dilga colliery are in a very serious condition in a Timisoara hospital, the paper says. Three miners died.
- Parliament will interview today Radu Onofrei and Dumitru Ceausu, nominated as Romania's ambassadors to London and respectively, to Paris.

- The newspaper runs an interview with Stefan Broasca, editor of the "Plai romanesc" newspaper from the Ukrainian city of Chernivtsi, who says that Ukrainian nationalist passions calmed down after they adopted the constitution.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper reports on a fire at the Hotel Central in Ploiesti, which was put out after four hours on Wednesday.
- Whatever is planted after May 21, when Orthodox Romanians celebrate the holiday of saints Constantin and Elena, will wilt before the autumn, according to old tradition, the paper says.
- The health ministry plans to pension off 27,000 administrative staff from the health sector by June 1.
ZIUA

- Ion Mihai Pacepa a former Securitate General who defected to the United States in the 1970s, says the former communists hired Arab terrorists to beat leading Romanian dissidents who had fled to the West.
- After refurbishing, the Hotel Rex in Mamaia, on the Black Sea coast, will be Romania's only five-star hotel, the newspaper says.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
